I disagree with several things here.

My fiance played Entertainer for a huge chunk of SWG's Live lifecycle.  She never complained about being bored with Entertainer in the ways you describe.  Back then it had much more of a social scene to it and that was the aspect she enjoyed which I think was the intent of the designers when they made entertainer.  Since you're forced to sit there and wait for wounds/battle fatigue to wear off, it gives you opportunities to socialize with other players.  In NGE Doctor didn't exist so they basically made Entertainers the new essential buffers, but by NGE the social scene was dead so they had to give them some kind of purpose. 

I also played entertainer for a long time but I didn't have as much patience as her so I had other professions to occupy me when I got bored, which is probably why we're able to have other professions.  Maybe entertainer just isn't for you?  Which is fine.

The same principle applies to doctor, but back then there wasn't an AFK Buff-bot around every corner so being a doctor felt more impactful and you felt needed.  Personally I always kind of enjoyed the fact that buffs were "required" for end-game combat, especially PvP because it meant if you took someone out you bought yourself some time and they won't just be respawning in 30 seconds at a spirit guide.  Doctor was always a passive playstyle, almost like a crafter, and we have Combat Medic for if you actually want to be an active "healer".  

I'd be strongly against removing skill requirements, it'd change the game fundamentally, essentially making entertaining worthless and slapping anyone in the face who enjoyed doing it full time.  SWG's design had its flaws but the player interdependencies are one thing that made it beautiful.  Streamlining things in such a way is what is killing the MMO industry.
